selection.basis: The completed L11 cap diagnostic shows strong cap sensitivity of the convergence flag but identical logical-failure counts at caps 80, 160, and 320. A fresh L11/L13 wave is therefore the cheapest direct test of whether the unresolved L9/L11 topology persists at larger size under the unchanged primary decoder.
selection.why_these_q_values: q=0.85, 0.90, and 0.95 are all unresolved in the 20-cluster refinement and jointly cover the finite-side guard, former transition endpoint, and former ceiling-side guard without inventing a midpoint classification.
selection.why_these_p_values: Reusing the seven-point high-p grid gives a directly comparable topology test across every earlier crossing and high-p sentinel while avoiding selection on the new L13 outcomes.
selection.why_fresh_clusters: Twenty new seed trajectories prevent pooling with either the five-cluster skeleton or the earlier 20-cluster L7/L9/L11 refinement and provide the registered unit for fluctuation-aware central-90% inference.
selection.claim_boundary: This wave can update only the decoder-specific L11/L13 finite-size topology. It cannot alone establish p_c(q), q_c, authorize q=0.925, change the primary cap, or expand to square.

verification.syndrome_fidelity_and_source_stability: fail-closed in the shard runner and analyzer

next_transition: Launch the three bounded q shards with three workers. Validate all 168000 raw records and analyze the L11/L13 topology before q=0.925 or square.
